title: NO COMPARISON to standard dehumidifiers in high humidity situations.
text: NO COMPARISON to standard dehumidifiers in high humidity situations.. Anyone who has rated this as getting the job done has probably never owned a true dehumidifier.  I ordered for a very VERY small bathroom (50 sf) that has a stand up shower.  We've just moved in recently, and this one bathroom doesn't have an exhaust fan.  I have a regular dehumidifier (50 pint capacity, I believe) and I've had whole house dehumidifiers; with those, I could get in the hot shower and when I stepped out the bathroom would be fog-free.  First time I used the Eva-dry I left the bathroom door open and when I stepped out, the whole bathroom was layered in moisture...literally! droplets were forming on the bottom of the wall cabinet.  I left the Eva-dry running (we never turned it off from the night before, when we'd first plugged it in) and after an hour and a half the bathroom was finally dry.  (Don't assume:  This period is the normal dry time without ANYTHING in the bathroom.)  The next time I got in the shower, I closed the bathroom door and kept it closed.  It took over 3 hours for the Eva-dry to dehumidify to the point that there were no longer droplets on the bottom of the wall cabinet, but the mirror was still coated in thick, wet 'fog'.  I've since replaced the Eva-dry with our huge (to me, and certainly by comparison) Hauer 50 Pint and when I get out of the shower the bathroom is dry and I don't have to wipe the mirror dry. *** Might be worth mentioning that I live in Georgia and I purchased/used the Eva-dry in August, which is possibly the most humid month of the year here.

Portable Dehumidifier for Bedroom: With a compact size of 6.5X5.3X8.5 inch it is very convenient to be placed anywhere. Helping to get the excess moisture out of the air for you in bedroom, bathroom, RV, closet and more.
